I was fixing my hair in the school bathroom mirror, nervous about my first day at a brand new school,
when through the reflection, I saw a couple of kids creeping up behind me, holding an entire
toilet bowl over my head. Before I could even turn around, they dumped it, caca and pee-pee
pouring down on me, soaking my best outfit. My face burned, my first day already ruined.
The biggest kid leaned in. Welcome to my school, new kid. Try to get me in trouble,
I'm untouchable. He was only targeting me because I was new, but if he wanted to pull pranks,
I'd pull the biggest one he ever saw. So I walked out dripping, looking for a teacher
to snitch on him, and the kids I'd hoped to befriend gagged and pinched their noses.
Caca boy! He smells like doo-doo! People pressed against the lockers just to avoid me.
When I tried to explain to a teacher, she plugged her nose and marched me straight to
the principal's office. He took one whiff and shot up from his chair. It's your first day
and you're already pulling pranks like this? Get out of my school. Suspended, just like that,
without a single word from me. As I walked out, I spotted the bully leaning against the wall,
laughing. Told you I'm untouchable. He turned and walked off like he'd already won,
but I knew exactly what I was going to do. The next morning, I snuck in before sunrise
and rigged every toilet.
Tying a rope to the water main so one pull would blow them all. Then I hid in a stall
and waited. Hours later, the bully strolled in and started fixing his hair in the mirror.
I stepped out, and he smirked. I thought they suspended you, caca boy. You want round
two that bad? I just grinned and yanked the rope. The pipes rumbled while he stood there
confused, so I bolted out and locked the door, trapping him inside as every toilet erupted
at once. The whole school shook, and he came blasting into the hallway, covered in caca
head to toe. He blew up the bathroom! A kid screamed. The principal ran over, so I shrugged.
I tried to stop him, but he didn't. I tried to stop him, but he didn't. I tried to stop
him. He was pulling the same prank as yesterday, but it backfired. He suspended the bully on
the spot and welcomed me back. By lunch, nobody called me caca boy anymore. They were too
busy laughing at diarrhea boy.
